routes.reason: Accept. PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIArithmeticDModules is proposed as a Part II of PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology, and the title reproduces the parent's exactly before the colon ('P-adic differential equations, rigid cohomology and p-adic weights, Part II: arithmetic D-modules, the six operations and geometric Satake'), as PROTOCOL section 15 requires. It is not a rival roadmap: the same Part II, with the same parent, is already proposed by PAPER-XU-ZHU-22, so this extraction joins an existing proposal rather than opening a competing one. The parent, checked in data/atlas.json, runs RD.0-RD.7 through Robba-ring and p-adic-weight theory and stops short of Berthelot's arithmetic D-modules; the six operations for D^dagger-modules on realizable schemes and stacks, which sections 1-2 of this paper build, are genuinely beyond it.

Accept. GlobalShtukasPartIICrystallineCompanions is a Part II of GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands and reproduces the parent's title verbatim before the colon. The parent's stages GS.0-GS.7 are ell-adic throughout - shtukas, the cohomology of moduli of shtukas, excursion operators and the ell-adic Langlands parametrisation - and an atlas-wide search for 'isocrystal', 'companion' and 'overconvergent' returns nothing that covers this paper's subject (the only 'companion' hits are the Tau Ceti companion lemmas and automorphic material). So the p-adic Langlands correspondence for overconvergent F-isocrystals and the existence of crystalline companions for curves are not claimed anywhere in the atlas, and a Part II is the right home for them.

notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-39fac3 (issue #1430). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in its files.

Provenance. Both recorded hashes match byte for byte: the arXiv v3 PDF b890ef13...f8c8dd29 (134 pp.) and the v3 e-print 78bbf4b8...9e00c7bc (a single gzipped pcc.tex, 13309 lines, with Shift-JIS comments that make grep treat it as binary - it has to be read with an explicit decoder). The published JAMS text is paywalled (HTTP 403), as the extraction records, so all findings are against v3, which postdates acceptance.

Numbering and coverage. Eight theorem environments share the counter that plain subsubsection headings also advance, and the appendix letters it. Simulating that independently gives 243 numbered objects, and the appendix comes out lettered A, matching the extraction's A.2.1-A.2.4 and A.3.2 locators exactly - a check worth making, since a paper with a single appendix can number it either way. Coverage is complete: the ten objects not named in any locator are nine bare subsubsection headings and one remark.

Statuses. The single planned item cites GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.6 and :GS.2, both of which exist in data/atlas.json. There are no library items, which is right for this subject.

Routes. Two Part II routes, both accepted; see the route verdicts.

Mistakes in the paper. All 27 were read at their locators in pcc.tex and all 27 quote the source verbatim (E7 writes varphi where the paper writes phi; nothing else differs). All 27 are accepted. Several are settled by the paper against itself: E1, where the Corollary writes the multiplicity of E'(-t) while the Proposition it is drawn from writes E'(t) at the same point; E15, where Tr_f lies in Ext^0 and so comes from E_1^{0,0}, not p = 1; E22, where the appendix's own L-function det(1 - Z^{deg(x)}F_x)^{-1} shows that F_x is the q^{deg x}-Frobenius, so the trace formula's sum over X(k_n) needs F_x^{n/deg x}; and E10, where section 1.5.7 speaks of '(Var 2) and (Var 3)' holding 'when the homomorphisms in the diagrams are defined', which is the missing hypothesis. Three were settled by computation: E4, where the comparison map for the Dwork module is exp((omega - 1)pi x), whose coefficients have absolute value p^{-s_p(n)/(p-1)} and do not tend to 0, so the displayed isomorphism does not exist; E24, where Spec F_{q^2} over F_q at n = 2 makes the trace formula read 2 = 0; and E13, where the E_1 weight bound falls short of what the abutment needs by the simplicial index.

One correction in place. E4's affects was 'nothing'; I set it to 'the proof'. The display is the whole justification of Remark 1.1.2, and the remark is invoked inside the proof of Lemma 1.4.11 ('By Remark \ref{Frobnotdep}, we get (i)'). The remark's conclusion still stands, and the entry's own repair is a reasonable route to it, but it is a sketch - it needs sigma to normalise Aut(K/Frac W(k)) and the twisted product to collapse - and the review says so.

Two entries I accepted with a reservation recorded in their review reason rather than by editing them: E10, whose counterexample depends on reading 'flat of relative dimension d' fibrewise-equidimensionally, which the definition of M_d does not settle (the finding survives on the author's own phrasing in 1.5.7), and E27, whose second clause about dim_L End(F) is correct but does not damage the proof of A.4.1, since the factor appears on both sides of the comparison and cancels.

Verdict: accept.
